Pane Toscano Baker's Percentage

One flour-dusted loaf of 960 g, with the salt left at zero. The rise runs fast and the crust tastes of wheat. Do not salt it back.

Detailed method

Salt is zero on purpose. The calculator opens at 500 g flour, 72% hydration, 20% starter, no salt, and no yeast. That is 360 g water and 100 g starter, 960 g of dough. The starter is itself 100% hydration, the same assumption used for effective hydration. The page shows 74.5% effective hydration. The balls fields open at 1 loaf of 960 g. With no salt the rise runs faster, and the crust tastes of wheat. Leave the salt out. These times assume you only change the flour amount and keep the percentages the same. Still judge the dough by how it looks and feels.

  1. Starter Use 100 g of starter that is bubbly and has about doubled. That starter is part of the gram total. Do not add instant yeast, and do not add salt. Both fields stay at zero.
  2. Mix Stir 500 g flour, 360 g water, and the 100 g starter until no dry flour remains. At 72% with no salt the dough feels slack. Aim for about 24°C (75°F).
  3. Bulk Cover it at about 24°C (75°F). With no salt it moves faster than a salted loaf. Give it three gentle folds in the first 90 minutes, then leave it until it has grown by about half, often 2 to 3 hours from the mix. If the top starts to sink, shape it.
  4. Shape Dust the counter and the dough with flour. Tighten the whole 960 g into one oval. This batch is one loaf. The flour on the skin is a light dusting and is not part of the gram total.
  5. Proof Set it seam-side up in a floured basket, or seam-side down on a cloth. Cover it for 40 to 60 minutes, until it looks puffy. Do not let it collapse.
  6. Bake Heat the oven to 230°C (450°F) with a lidded pot, or with a tray of hot water for steam. Score once. Bake 20 minutes with the steam, then 20 to 25 minutes more at 200°C (390°F), until the crust is deep gold and firm.
  7. Cool Set it on a rack for at least 1 hour before you slice. The photo shows that floury crust. It shows two loaves. This batch makes one.
